title: parse.rs accesses message.parts[0] without bounds check
description: parse.rs line 28: extract_headers(&message.parts[0], raw) indexes parts[0] directly. MessageParser::default().parse(raw).ok_or(ParseError::NoHeaders)? guards against None, but not against an empty parts vec. If mail-parser returns Some(message) with parts.is_empty(), this panics. Trigger: a malformed message that mail-parser partially parses (returning Some) but produces zero parts. This is undocumented behaviour of mail-parser; the safe guard is to check parts.is_empty() and return ParseError::NoHeaders.
